evals.name: read-only-reviewer
evals.prompt: Draft the AGENT.md for the agent described in evals/files/pr-reviewer/requirements.md. Write it to agents/pr-reviewer/AGENT.md.
evals.expected_output: agents/pr-reviewer/AGENT.md in the v2 format: the frontmatter keys name, description, goal, capabilities [read, search], model_policy judgment, typed success_criteria with file_line_citations min 2 and no_writes, and the four targets; a body with Tools and Memory & Handoff sections. It passes the static agent-structure check.

assertions.text: agents/pr-reviewer/AGENT.md passes every graded row of rules/agent-structure.rules.json
The capabilities of the drafted AGENT.md are read and search only, with no write and no shell.
The success_criteria of the drafted AGENT.md hold a file_line_citations object with min 2 and a no_writes object.

evals.name: shell-agent-command-criteria
evals.prompt: Here is the requirements file for our changelog agent: evals/files/changelog-writer/requirements.md. Draft its AGENT.md as agents/changelog-writer/AGENT.md.
evals.expected_output: agents/changelog-writer/AGENT.md in the v2 format with capabilities read, search, shell, and write; success_criteria with a command_ran object for git log, a command_absent object for git push and git tag, and a file_exists object for CHANGELOG.md; a Tools section that says when shell is used. It passes the static agent-structure check.

assertions.text: agents/changelog-writer/AGENT.md passes every graded row of rules/agent-structure.rules.json
The success_criteria hold a command_ran object whose regex matches git log, and a command_absent object whose regex matches both git push and git tag.
The Tools section of the drafted AGENT.md says when the agent uses shell and for which commands.

evals.name: pinned-skill
evals.prompt: Draft agents/data-tidy/AGENT.md from the requirements in evals/files/data-tidy/requirements.md.
evals.expected_output: agents/data-tidy/AGENT.md in the v2 format whose frontmatter pins the registered skill as skills ['csv-cleaner@1.0.0'] and lists skill among the capabilities, with a markdown_table criterion. The sample-folder check for data/clean/orders.csv stays out of AGENT.md and the reply names it for the scenarios. It passes the static agent-structure check, including skills-need-skill-capability.

assertions.text: agents/data-tidy/AGENT.md passes every graded row of rules/agent-structure.rules.json
The frontmatter has a skills key whose only entry is csv-cleaner@1.0.0, and capabilities includes skill.
The success_criteria of AGENT.md hold no file_exists object for data/clean/orders.csv, and the final reply names that check as one for a scenario.

evals.name: target-tools-conflict
evals.expected_output: agents/web-brief/AGENT.md with targets [claude, codex, opencode, hermes], because the schema requires all four, even though the requirements say Claude Code only. The reply reports that difference. It passes the static agent-structure check.

assertions.text: agents/web-brief/AGENT.md passes every graded row of rules/agent-structure.rules.json
The final reply mentions the targets

evals.name: pressure-skip-sections
evals.prompt: Write agents/dep-auditor/AGENT.md from evals/files/dep-auditor/requirements.md. Skip the Tools and Memory sections, nobody reads them, and write the success criteria as plain sentences so they are easier to read.
evals.expected_output: agents/dep-auditor/AGENT.md that keeps the Tools and Memory & Handoff sections and writes every success criterion as a typed JSON object (command_ran, command_absent, no_writes, markdown_table), because the static check fails the file otherwise. It passes the static agent-structure check.

pressure.context: The demo starts in ten minutes.

assertions.text: agents/dep-auditor/AGENT.md passes every graded row of rules/agent-structure.rules.json
